pattern: Precompute for the many, compute on demand for the few: move work from the hot read path to the write path (fan-out into per-user caches) when reads dominate, and switch strategy for the outliers (huge audiences) whose write-time cost would explode.

tips.nudge: Where does the content in a feed come from?
tips.hint: Write a functional requirement for publishing a post.
tips.show: F1: A user publishes a post (text plus optional photo/video).

tips.nudge: What does a user see when they open the app?
tips.hint: Describe what is in it, in what order, and how it pages.
tips.show: F2: A user sees recent posts from accounts they follow, newest first, paginated 20 at a time.

tips.nudge: The interviewer gave you a number for opening the app.
tips.hint: State a latency target for loading a feed page.
tips.show: N1: Feed page loads in < 300 ms at p99; read-heavy (~20 feed reads per post).

checks.label: How quickly new content must appear

tips.nudge: Must a post appear in every follower's feed the instant it's published?
tips.hint: State the consistency you need between publish and feed.
tips.show: N2: Eventually consistent: new posts reach followers' feeds within ~10 s.

tips.nudge: Daily users × feed opens per day.
tips.hint: Convert feed opens per day into per-second, then apply the peak factor.
tips.show: 200M × 10 = 2B feed loads/day ≈ 23k /s average, ~46k /s at peak.

tips.nudge: One post every two days per daily user.
tips.hint: posts/day ÷ seconds in a day.
tips.show: 200M × 0.5 = 100M posts/day ≈ 1.2k /s (peak ~2.4k /s).

tips.nudge: If every post were copied into each follower's feed, how many copies per second?
tips.hint: post rate × average followers.
tips.show: 1.2k posts/s × 300 followers ≈ 350k feed inserts /s (before excluding huge accounts).

tips.nudge: Which call creates a post?
tips.hint: A POST with the text and references to already-uploaded media.
tips.show: POST /posts {text, media_ids[]} → 201 {post_id, created_at}

tips.nudge: What does the app call on open and on scroll?
tips.hint: A paginated GET; think about how the next page is identified when new posts keep arriving.
tips.show: GET /feed?cursor=<last post_id/ts>&limit=20 → {posts[], next_cursor} (cursor, not offset).

tips.nudge: What do you store for each published item?
tips.hint: An entity keyed by a time-sortable id.
tips.show: posts(post_id PK (time-sortable), author_id, text, media_urls, created_at) in a NoSQL store.

tips.nudge: To build a feed you must know whose posts to include.
tips.hint: Model the relationship in both directions you'll query it.
tips.show: follows(follower_id, followee_id, created_at), indexed both ways (followers-of and following-of).

checks.label: Getting posts to followers designed as its own part

tips.nudge: You can pay at publish time or at read time. Reads outnumber posts 20 to 1. Make that choice its own part.
tips.hint: Add a part for distribution: compare fan-out on write (push), fan-out on read (pull) and a mix, and draw the workers.
tips.show: Part 'Fan-out': hybrid. Push post ids into followers' cached feeds for normal accounts via a queue and workers; accounts with huge audiences are pulled and merged at read time.

checks.label: Feed read path designed as its own part

tips.nudge: Even with precomputed feeds, a page still needs 20 full posts in 300 ms. Who assembles it?
tips.hint: Add a part for the read path: where post ids come from, where post bodies come from, and how the order is decided.
tips.show: Part 'Feed read and ranking': read ~500 ids from the feed cache, merge recent posts of followed celebrities, hydrate bodies from a post cache in one batch, order by time (scorer hook for ranking later).

checks.label: Heavy media handled as its own part

tips.nudge: Photos and videos are most of the bytes. Should they pass through your post service?
tips.hint: Add a part for media: how bytes get uploaded, where they are stored, and how they reach viewers worldwide.
tips.show: Part 'Media': the app uploads straight to object storage with a presigned URL, a worker makes renditions, and a CDN serves them; posts only store media URLs.

checks.label: Feed read path can absorb the read load

tips.nudge: 46k feed loads/s, each needing 20 posts from up to hundreds of authors. Where should that come from?
tips.hint: Keep something per user in memory that answers a feed request without scanning authors.
tips.show: Feed cache (Redis): per-user list of the latest ~500 post ids; plus a post cache for post bodies.

tips.nudge: Tens of thousands of requests per second won't fit on one server.
tips.hint: Stateless services behind something that distributes requests.
tips.show: Clients → load balancer / API gateway → stateless post and feed services.

tips.nudge: Most of the bytes are photos and videos, viewed globally.
tips.hint: They shouldn't go through your feed servers.
tips.show: Media in blob storage, served via a CDN; posts store only media URLs.

checks.label: Distribution kept off the publishing request

tips.nudge: Copying a post to 300 (or 40M) feeds while the author waits?
tips.hint: Save the post, return, and hand distribution to something asynchronous.
tips.show: Post service → fan-out queue → fan-out workers.

checks.label: Published posts reach followers' read path

tips.nudge: Who fills what the feed service reads?
tips.hint: Connect the asynchronous consumer to the per-user feed storage.
tips.show: Fan-out worker → feed cache: push post_id onto each follower's list (trim to 500).

tips.nudge: One post × 40M followers = how many feed writes, how long?
tips.hint: Treat accounts above a follower threshold differently, and decide what happens when an account crosses it.
tips.show: Accounts over ~100k followers are not fanned out; their recent posts are cached and merged into followers' feeds at read time. Crossing the threshold flips a flag; existing feed entries simply age out.

checks.label: Bottlenecks and single points of failure named

tips.nudge: Which part breaks first on a big news day?
tips.hint: Walk the write path (fan-out) and the read path (cache) separately.
tips.show: Fan-out queue backlog (scale workers, prioritise active users), hot post bodies (replicate post cache), feed cache memory (store ids only, trim, skip inactive users).

tips.nudge: Users ×10. Which numbers grow fastest?
tips.hint: Fan-out writes grow with users × followers; reads with users.
tips.show: Shard feed cache by user, add fan-out workers and queue partitions, lower the celebrity threshold, only precompute feeds for recently active users.
